claim_verdicts.evidence: "An RBAC Role or ClusterRole contains rules that represent a set of permissions." "A Role always sets permissions within a particular namespace; when you create a Role, you have to specify the namespace it belongs in."

PolicyRule: apiGroups — "If multiple API groups are specified, any action requested against one of the enumerated resources in any API group will be allowed." verbs — "verbs is a list of Verbs that apply to ALL the ResourceKinds contained in this rule."

"A role binding grants the permissions defined in a role to a user or set of users. It holds a list of subjects (users, groups, or service accounts), and a reference to the role being granted." "A RoleBinding may reference any Role in the same namespace." The lesson's 'users or groups' omits service accounts, which depth_notes defers to the next lesson; not wrong.

Round 2 (text now names API group, resource, verb and binding namespace). rbac.md: "Permissions are purely additive (there are no \"deny\" rules)." PolicyRule lists apiGroups, resources and verbs as the parts of a rule. authorization.md: "If all modules have no opinion on the request, then the request is denied. An overall deny verdict means that the API server rejects the request and responds with an HTTP 403 (Forbidden) status."

Follows directly from "Permissions are purely additive (there are no \"deny\" rules)": a second Role can only add permissions, so a granted right disappears only when the granting binding/Role is removed or narrowed. rbac-good-practices.md also speaks of rights that are "revoked by removing RoleBindings or ClusterRoleBindings".

Labelled as opinion in the lesson's framing; supported by "Ideally, minimal RBAC rights should be assigned to users and service accounts. Only permissions explicitly required for their operation should be used." and "Assign permissions at the namespace level where possible." The 'cannot be narrowed by another rule' reason follows from the no-deny rule.

Round 2 (adds API group definition). Docs example Role: "- apiGroups: [\"\"] # \"\" indicates the core API group / resources: [\"pods\"]". rbac.md: "RBAC refers to resources using exactly the same name that appears in the URL". 'A named set of resource kinds' is definitional for the group.
"GET, HEAD | get (for individual resources), list (for collections, including full object content), watch (for watching an individual resource or collection of resources)".

Docs RoleBinding example: "subjects: - kind: User / name: jane / apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io / roleRef: kind: Role / name: pod-reader / apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io". authentication.md: "Kubernetes does not have objects which represent normal user accounts."
